# Database workshop

Splitting customer details into a customer table prevents the same address being copied into every order.

A foreign key connects an order to an existing customer record.

Third normal form removes dependencies between non-key attributes.

Database performance memo

A B-tree index helps locate records without scanning every row.

Extra indexes consume disk space and make inserts more expensive.

The slow-query exercise uses the identifier DB-LAB-27.

Fictional purchase receipt

Receipt LAMP-450 records a desk lamp purchase for 450 INR.

The lamp warranty covers manufacturing defects for twelve months.

Keep the receipt to request a replacement for a faulty switch.

Fictional laptop receipt

Receipt LAP-450 records a laptop purchase for 45000 INR.

The laptop warranty lasts twenty-four months from purchase.

Accidental liquid damage is excluded from this warranty.

# River project meeting

The River prototype review moved from Tuesday to Thursday at 15:00.

Mira owns the accessibility review, including keyboard navigation.

Dev will replace the placeholder charts before the prototype review.

# Fictional hill-station trip

Train booking TRIP-271 departs at 06:20 from platform four.

The homestay keeps luggage before the 14:00 check-in time.

Pack a waterproof jacket because the walking route has no covered shelter.

Community garden notes

Water the tomato beds near sunrise to reduce evaporation.

Yellow lower leaves together with wet soil can indicate excessive watering.

Compost is mixed into the beds before planting seedlings.

# Team backup exercise

The exercise keeps three copies of each file on two types of storage, with one copy off-site.

A restore drill checks that archived files can actually be recovered.

The recovery drill is scheduled for the first Friday of each month.

Fictional sales summary

Quarterly revenue fell from 120000 INR to 90000 INR after the campus kiosk closed.

Online orders rose while walk-in purchases declined.

The summary is filed under report code SALES-Q2-18.

# Study routine

Retrieval practice means answering from memory before checking the notes.

Spacing revision sessions over several days improves the study routine compared with one long session.

The practice quiz identifier is STUDY-83.

# Fictional workshop handbook

## Arrival and room preparation
Participants enter through the courtyard and collect a printed schedule from the welcome desk. The room coordinator checks that each table has paper, pencils and a reusable name card. Chairs are arranged in small groups so participants can discuss their drafts without moving across the room. The welcome session introduces the facilitators and explains where coats and bags can be left. The first activity is a short observation exercise using everyday objects placed on the tables.

## Materials and session rhythm
The workshop alternates quiet individual work with short group discussions. Facilitators collect unused materials between sessions and return reusable supplies to labelled boxes. Participants are encouraged to keep rough sketches as well as finished pages so they can explain how an idea changed. During the afternoon session, each group selects one draft to present to the room. The coordinator checks the projector before presentations begin and leaves a printed alternative at the front desk in case the display fails.

## Feedback and closing preparation
Feedback cards ask participants to describe one useful activity and one confusing instruction. Facilitators read the cards after the event rather than interrupting the final exercise. Completed sketches are placed on a shared display table for a short walking review. The room coordinator checks the attendance sheet, sorts reusable materials and records any missing supplies. A separate closing note lists tasks that the next workshop team should review before booking the same room again.

## Closing logistics
The collection box for feedback cards is beside the west exit.

Borrowed drawing tablets must be returned to locker C-17.

The final room inspection starts at 18:40, after participants leave.

Fictional Lakeside project schedule

The Lakeside prototype review is on Tuesday at 15:00. Omar owns its keyboard review. This schedule belongs to Lakeside, not River.

Archived fictional train booking

TRIP-270 departs at 08:10 from platform two. This is the previous booking and does not describe TRIP-271.

Fictional stationery stock report

Stock increased from 90000 to 120000 units. These figures count items held in the warehouse; they are not quarterly revenue.
